input.quote: (c) Removal. If a Servicer Termination Event occurs and is continuing, the Indenture Trustee may and, if directed by the Noteholders of a majority of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class, must remove the Servicer and terminate its rights and obligations under this Agreement by notifying the Servicer, the Issuer, the Parent Support Provider, the Owner Trustee, and the Secured Parties.
input.rationale: Counterparty side is better than our preferred position: Section 7.1 bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer except where legally unable to perform, and Section 7.3 requires it to keep performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement, so there is no Vendor termination-for-convenience right. However, on our side the only route to remove the Servicer is Section 7.2(c) for a Servicer Termination Event (i.e. for cause), and the Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated (Section 8.3) — well beyond 12 months. The Optional Acquisition/Clean-Up Redemption (Section 8.1) and Optional Redemption (Section 8.2) are held by the Class A Certificateholder, defined as "the Originators or their designee" (counterparty-side), and require agreement on the Optional Acquisition Amount, so they are not a customer convenience exit. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months fails the fallback, so we have added a 30-day no-fee convenience termination right, conditioned on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement under Section 7.4 to preserve servicing continuity for the Noteholders.

proposal.summary: Add an Issuer right to terminate the Servicer for convenience on 30 days' notice, without fee, subject to Successor Servicer continuity
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article VII lets the Servicer be removed only for a Servicer Termination Event, leaving us with no no-fault exit over a multi-year engagement, so we have added a 30-day convenience termination right with a refund of prepaid amounts and no termination fee. We have preserved servicing continuity by conditioning effectiveness on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement under Section 7.4; if 30 days is too short we can live with 60 days' notice.

ops.text: Section 7.2A Termination for Convenience by the Issuer. In addition to and without limiting the rights set forth in Section 7.2, the Issuer may terminate the rights and obligations of the Servicer (including in its capacity as Custodian) under this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time and without cause, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, the Parent Support Provider, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee. No termination fee, penalty or other compensation will be payable by the Issuer in connection with such termination, other than Servicing Fees accrued and unpaid for services performed through the effective date of termination, and the Servicer will refund to the Issuer any amounts prepaid in respect of the period after such effective date. Any such termination will become effective on the date stated in the notice of termination, but not before a Successor Servicer has accepted its engagement under Section 7.4, and Sections 7.3, 7.4 and 7.5 will apply to any termination under this Section 7.2A.
